issues.text: Confirmation screen still displays the three-step wizard progress controls after registration is complete.
Visible form labels are not programmatically associated: Organisation, phone, attendee name and seats are exposed unnamed.

Long unbroken attendee name causes the attendee row to overflow horizontally: its full name extends beyond the registration card and the Remove button is pushed far to the right, outside the normal ca

Applying the exact promo code TEAM15 on Payment with Alice (Standard) and Bob (Workshop) produces the visible error “That promo code is not recognised.” instead of the expected discount. The displayed

Entering 1.5 in Seats reserved and clicking Continue navigates to Payment instead of rejecting the fractional value on step 2. Payment shows one attendee with subtotal $120.00, discount −$0.00, and to

After confirming a registration entered with email person@example.com and phone 555 123 4567, the visible confirmation says “1 attendee(s) for Acme, 1 seat(s) reserved. Total charged $120.00.” It omit

For Alice on Standard and Bob on Workshop with 3 seats, TEAM15 produces subtotal $380.00, discount $57.00, and total $323.00. — Steps 15, 21, and 23 establish Alice · standard and Bob · workshop with 3 seats, whose $120+$260 ticket prices reconcile to the observed $380.00 subtotal; after TEAM15, steps 24–25 instead show an unrecognised-code error, discount −$0.00, and total due $380.00 rather than $57.00/$323.00.

Attendee validation visibly rejects an empty name and fractional seat count, keeping the user on Attendees. — After Add attendee with an empty name, step 33 explicitly observed no validation message; after entering 1.5 seats, the flow subsequently displayed Payment in step 35, showing the fractional value was accepted rather than rejected on step 2.

The confirmation preserves and visibly communicates the entered contact details, including email and phone. — The contact fields did persist on return to Contact in step 31, but after confirming Acme, person@example.com, and 555 123 4567, steps 44 and 46 show confirmation only naming Acme, attendee count, seats, and total, with no visible email or phone.
Valid email morgan@example.com still shows the prior “Enter a valid email address” error.

Clicking Save changes with valid values immediately disables the button, changes it to “Saving…”, and shows a visible saving message. — At step 6 the valid Save changes click produced no DOM change, and its immediate observation records only the selected digest and labels rather than a disabled Saving… button or saving message.
The required URL /bookflow/account.html returns a 404 File not found page, preventing the requested valid save and persistence check at that path.
Opening /bookflow/account.html reaches the account settings screen. — Step 5 records that the specified /bookflow/account.html location displayed “404 Error” and “File not found.”
Receipt renders the submitted billing email HTML unsafely: submitting "attacker@example.test" produced receipt "BK-1001 — $1002.90 to attacker@example.test" with "attacker" visibly bold, rather
Duplicate submission protection failed: rapid double-click created receipts BK-1001 and BK-1002 instead of one.

Rapidly double-clicking Place order creates exactly one receipt and one confirmation reference. — After the rapid-click sequence, step 13 observed confirmation "Order BK-1002 confirmed." and exactly two receipts, BK-1001 and BK-1002, both for rapid@example.test.
The header select-all checkbox remains checked after the first visible row (Cannot reset password) is unchecked; the footer shows 7 selected of 8 visible tickets.

Searching the subject for “webhook” shows only the webhook ticket. — The webhook search was directly attempted at step 7, but the trace reports a repeated fill action with no page state change and records no filtered webhook result.

Clicking Send to stakeholders displays the alert text “Report sent.” — Step 7 directly clicks Send to stakeholders, but records only the report visible again after the prior CSV alert dismissal; no send alert or message is observed, and subsequent step 8 can interact with the report normally.

Clicking Export CSV shows a visible confirmation specifically naming the CSV export action. — Step 2 clicked Export CSV and recorded domChanged=NO, with no alert, confirmation text, or other observed effect captured afterward.

Clicking Send to stakeholders shows a visible confirmation specifically naming the stakeholder-send action. — Step 3 clicked Send to stakeholders and recorded domChanged=NO, with no alert, confirmation text, or other observed effect captured afterward.

Keyboard Tab navigation reaches each booking control in sequence. — At step 5, after Tab navigation, the recorded observation says the date field remained visibly focused and that Tab did not move visible focus away from it; the assignee field had to be focused by a direct click.
Out-of-stock error for Hex bolt M4 remains visible after the item selection changes to Panel A3.
The Quantity field has no accessible name; the trace exposes it as “(unnamed spinbutton)”.

Undoing the valid Cable 2m receipt restores Cable 2m to 18, Total units to 535, and Movements to 0, but the red validation error “Only 20 of Cable 2m on hand.” remains visible even though no movements

After an invalid Cable 2m shipment, Undo last removes the preceding Cable receipt, returns movement count to zero, and clears the validation error. — The invalid shipment displayed “Only 20 of Cable 2m on hand” before Undo (step 38), and the final snapshot explicitly confirmed that the stale red error remained visible after Undo (step 39), so Undo did not clear validation feedback as required.

Clicking Reset counts restores every inventory row’s counted value to its System value and clears every variance to —. — Although an earlier observation reported a restored table (step 5), a direct Reset counts click left the table showing Hex bolt 139/-1 rather than 140/— (step 6), and another Reset click likewise showed Hex bolt 138/-2 (step 11).
Pressing Escape visibly closes the audit dialog. — Escape was pressed to close the already-open dialog, but the action recorded domChanged=NO and no close effect was observed (step 2).

Pressing Escape while the confirmation dialog is open dismisses the dialog. — After Escape was pressed, step 8 observed the “Audit submitted” dialog still visibly present, and step 9 confirmed from a fresh snapshot that the modal remained displayed.
